literal_meaning: নাড়ী বা শিরা বাঁধা (tying the vein or pulse)
figurative_meaning_en: Beginning formal apprenticeship or training under a music guru
similar_in_english: Sitting at the feet of the master
Taking up the mantle of apprenticeship
example_sentences_in_bangla: তার বয়স এগারো বছরের সময় গুরুর কাছে নাড়া বাঁধা হয়েছে।
ঐতিহ্যবাহী সঙ্গীতশিক্ষায় নাড়া বাঁধা একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অনুষ্ঠান।
example_sentences_in_english: At the age of eleven, he underwent naada baandha under his guru.
In traditional music education, tying the naada is an important initiation ceremony.
history: This idiom originates from the ancient guru-shishya parampara in Indian classical music, where the guru ties a sacred thread on the disciple's wrist to mark the start of formal training, symbolizing commitment and the beginning of the musical journey.
note: Refers specifically to the ceremonial initiation in Hindustani or Carnatic music traditions prevalent in Bengal.
